h1: Subcutaneous injection sites: where weekly injections go, and what the trials specified
dek: A subcutaneous injection goes into the fat under the skin, usually in the abdomen, thigh or upper arm. This page sets out what weekly pen labels, CDC guidance and patient instructions say, and what the cagrilintide trials specified.
scope: Informational only. No dosing instructions, no vendors or prices.

competitors.gap: Generic syringe instructions; nothing on once-weekly pens, label-stated site rules or who may inject into the back of the arm
competitors.source: Semrush top-10; not fetched (content confirmed via search excerpts)

competitors.gap: Arthritis-drug context; no GLP-1 pen labels and no trial information
Prefilled syringe only; no comparison of syringe angle with pen technique
Vaccine-only; does not cover weekly self-injected medicines

information_gain: The only page on this SERP that puts the site rules of the approved weekly GLP-1 pens (abdomen, thigh, back of upper arm by another person, weekly rotation, site change without dose change) next to the CDC syringe angle and states what the cagrilintide/CagriSema trials actually specified, including the separate pens in phase 2 and the dual-chamber pen usability results.
serp_format_rewarded: Image pack, video carousel and featured snippet: a short definition, a captioned site table and a numbered step list win the snippet; PAA on site, angle and SC vs IM is answered in the FAQ.
